dod_intent_evidence: $749,044 Air Force Phase II SBIR (2022) explicitly tasked to support Department of the Air Force Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Response (HADR) missions — SBIR abstract section.
score_evidence: "Spectral Analysis that sees deep within your imagery to find hidden insights using advanced Deep Learning algorithms." → lab_language_intensity

"Our proposed HSI technologies were initially built for the Precision Agriculture and Smart City markets for real-time, in situ collection, processing, analysis and dissemination to the user for rapid decision-making." → deployment_awareness_absence (civilian-market sensor architecture repurposed for DAF HADR with no re-engineering language)

"Other uses-cases for the technology include the location and identification of items of clothing and injured personnel (Search and Rescue)" → operator_absence (some mission/responder awareness present but framed generically, not centered on the operator)
employees(LI): 3, company founded ~2015, still SBIR/R&D-stage on this line 11 years later → stage_pressure (chronically small team, single-grant dependency)

blind_spots.blind_spot: HSI sensors were built for precision agriculture and smart-city 'real-time, in situ' cloud dissemination, then pitched for DAF disaster-response missions with no re-engineering language.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Sensor architecture optimized for row-crop imaging over a farm doesn't survive rotor wash, dust, and dirty power on an eVTOL platform in an actual disaster zone — no SWaP-C adaptation is described for the new use case.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Tiny 3-4 person team is repurposing an existing commercial product line for a new SBIR opportunity rather than building a purpose-built defense platform.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Our proposed HSI technologies were initially built for the Precision Agriculture and Smart City markets for real-time, in situ collection, processing, analysis and dissemination to the user for rapid decision-making.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Commercial product tiers ($20-$70/month, 10GB-250GB cloud storage) assume standard internet-connected cloud access.
blind_spots.operator_reality: HADR and DoD missions frequently operate in exactly the disconnected/degraded conditions a consumer cloud-storage subscription tier can't serve — no edge/on-device processing story is described anywhere.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Core commercial product (Spectralytics) was built as a SaaS analytics platform for civilian customers, not a field-deployed sensor payload.

blind_spots.blind_spot: SBIR abstract names the mission (stand-off HAZMAT detection for DAF HADR, logistical support response planning) but never names or describes who operates or interprets the sensor output in the field.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A stand-off detection capability is only as good as the operator's ability to interpret and act on it in real time — the abstract never identifies that operator or how they're trained on the tool.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team background (agriculture/geospatial data science) is centered on the sensing and analytics pipeline, not on end-user operations.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Hyperspectral imaging is the most effective remote sensing technology for stand-off HAZMAT detection.

opener_hook: Spectrabotics' $749K Air Force Phase II repurposes precision-agriculture hyperspectral sensors for disaster-response missions — the same sensor architecture built for real-time cloud dissemination on a farm.
what_they_do: Small hyperspectral-imaging and geospatial-analytics shop; repurposing agriculture/smart-city sensor tech for an Air Force-funded disaster-response (HADR) drone payload.
